svg.aria-label: Presence detection algorithm, stage by stage

g.text: How the camera decides someone is there
Five stages per frame, no image is ever stored, and two earlier designs failed on real hardware before this one worked.
A cell counts only if it
The whole decision, in five lines
val globalShift = sumDelta.toDouble() / cur.size // whole-frame drift
for (i in cur.indices) if (abs((cur[i] - prev[i]) - globalShift) > 45) changed++ // local only
WHY IT IS BUILT THIS WAY: TWO FAILED DESIGNS
A person is small in frame. Averaging change over all 768
cells diluted a real hand wave down to almost nothing, so
it never crossed any usable threshold.
Mains lighting flickers at 50 or 60 Hz and beats against the
camera frame rate. The WHOLE frame brightens and darkens
every frame, lighting up most cells. Read as constant motion.
Flicker moves every cell by the same amount, so it lives
entirely in the global shift. Remove that and only genuinely
LOCAL change survives, which is what a person actually is.
A faint wave far from a wide angle
No frame is ever decoded to an image, written to disk, or transmitted. What exists is 768 brightness numbers in memory,
overwritten on the very next frame. The camera permission is the only one the app requests, and denying it still leaves
a working clock that dims on a timer and wakes on tap.
